When reporting a problem, provide detailed information so we can assist you more effectively.\n    31→\n    32→## Setup\n    33→\n    34→Our environment setup is the same as the setup of the official [slime](https://github.com/THUDM/slime) framework. We use Docker:\n    35→\n    36→```bash\n    37→# Pull the image\n    38→docker pull slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126\n    39→\n    40→# Start the container\n    41→docker run -d --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \\\n    42→  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \\\n    43→  --name RLVE \\\n    44→  slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126 \\\n    45→  tail -f /dev/null\n    46→```\n    47→\n    48→After entering the Docker container, please follow these steps to clone the repository and install it:\n    49→\n    50→```bash\n    51→cd /root/\n    52→git clone https://github.com/Zhiyuan-Zeng/RLVE.git\n    53→cd RLVE\n    54→pip install -e .\n    55→```\n    56→\n    57→## Usage of Verifiable Environments in RLVE-Gym\n    58→\n    59→Each environment has an identifier, which you can find [here](Gym/environments/__init__.py). We take the following example:\n    60→\n    61→```python\n    62→identifier = \"Sorting\"\n    63→```\n    64→\n    65→Each environment has two classes - one for the environment itself and another for controlling the problem difficulty:\n    66→\n    67→```python\n    68→from Gym.environments import identifier2environment\n    69→from Gym.parameter_controllers import identifier2controller\n    70→\n    71→environment = identifier2environment[identifier]\n    72→controller_class = identifier2controller[identifier]\n    73→```\n    74→\n    75→Note that when creating the environment, you can specify the argument `answer_markers` to control how the answer is extracted from a model’s output during verification.\n    76→By default, it extracts the answer enclosed between `<answer>` and `</answer>`.\n    77→You can check [this example usage](slime/rollout/rm_hub/rlve_rm.py) for reference.\n    78→\n    79→When generating a problem, we specify a random seed `seed` and a problem difficulty level `d` ($d \\geq 0$):\n    80→\n    81→```python\n    82→import random\n    83→\n    84→seed = 42\n    85→\n    86→controller = controller_class()\n    87→d = 3\n    88→for _ in range(d) :\n    89→    controller.update()\n    90→\n    91→problem = environment()\n    92→parameter = random.choice(controller.get_parameter_list())\n    93→if problem.generator(seed = seed, parameter = parameter) :\n    94→    pass\n    95→else :\n    96→    problem = None\n    97→```\n    98→\n    99→Problem generation is successful when `problem` is not `None`.\n   100→\n   101→The input prompt is obtained via `problem.prompt_generator()`.  \n   102→The reward for a model output `output` is given by `problem.scorer(output)`, or you can access more detailed verification information using `problem.verifier(output)`.\n   103→\n   104→You can check [here](Gym/environment.py) for more detailed usage.\n   105→\n   106→## Model Download & Weight Conversion\n   107→\n   108→In the following, 155→**Warning:** Please make sure the weight conversion is successful before starting any training.\n   156→Even if the conversion fails, training can still launch without a runtime error, but the model will be trained from randomly initialized weights.\n   157→\n   158→\n   159→## Reward Shaping\n   160→\n   161→By default, we use the original reward provided by each verifiable environment as the reward used in the RL algorithm.  \n   162→Many environments employ continuous reward shaping, meaning that a model output can still receive a positive reward even if its answer is not fully correct.  \n   163→We found that when the training scale is small, using a binary reward can sometimes yield slightly better results (i.e., the model output receives 1 if and only if its answer is fully correct, and 0 otherwise).  \n   164→You can switch to binary rewards by changing `--reward-key reward` to `--reward-key accuracy` in `scripts/training/[MODEL]/rlve.sh`.\n   165→\n   166→## Wandb Setup\n   167→\n   168→To use Weights & Biases (wandb), please set your wandb API key in the environment variable `WANDB_API_KEY`.  \n   169→Alternatively, you can comment out the wandb-related arguments in `WANDB_ARGS` within the training script to disable wandb.\n   170→\n   171→## Environment Scaling\n   172→\n   173→You can run our environment scaling experiments as follows:\n   174→\n When reporting a problem, provide detailed information so we can assist you more effectively.\n\n## Setup\n\nOur environment setup is the same as the setup of the official [slime](https://github.com/THUDM/slime) framework. We use Docker:\n\n```bash\n# Pull the image\ndocker pull slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126\n\n# Start the container\ndocker run -d --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \\\n  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \\\n  --name RLVE \\\n  slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126 \\\n  tail -f /dev/null\n```\n\nAfter entering the Docker container, please follow these steps to clone the repository and install it:\n\n```bash\ncd /root/\ngit clone https://github.com/Zhiyuan-Zeng/RLVE.git\ncd RLVE\npip install -e .\n```\n\n## Usage of Verifiable Environments in RLVE-Gym\n\nEach environment has an identifier, which you can find [here](Gym/environments/__init__.py). We take the following example:\n\n```python\nidentifier = \"Sorting\"\n```\n\nEach environment has two classes - one for the environment itself and another for controlling the problem difficulty:\n\n```python\nfrom Gym.environments import identifier2environment\nfrom Gym.parameter_controllers import identifier2controller\n\nenvironment = identifier2environment[identifier]\ncontroller_class = identifier2controller[identifier]\n```\n\nNote that when creating the environment, you can specify the argument `answer_markers` to control how the answer is extracted from a model’s output during verification.\nBy default, it extracts the answer enclosed between `<answer>` and `</answer>`.\nYou can check [this example usage](slime/rollout/rm_hub/rlve_rm.py) for reference.\n\nWhen generating a problem, we specify a random seed `seed` and a problem difficulty level `d` ($d \\geq 0$):\n\n```python\nimport random\n\nseed = 42\n\ncontroller = controller_class()\nd = 3\nfor _ in range(d) :\n    controller.update()\n\nproblem = environment()\nparameter = random.choice(controller.get_parameter_list())\nif problem.generator(seed = seed, parameter = parameter) :\n    pass\nelse :\n    problem = None\n```\n\nProblem generation is successful when `problem` is not `None`.\n\nThe input prompt is obtained via `problem.prompt_generator()`.  \nThe reward for a model output `output` is given by `problem.scorer(output)`, or you can access more detailed verification information using `problem.verifier(output)`.\n\nYou can check [here](Gym/environment.py) for more detailed usage.\n\n## Model Download & Weight Conversion\n\nIn the following, we assume you are on a node with 8 GPUs, each equipped with at least 80GB of memory.\nWe recommend using H100 or H200 GPUs over A100s, due to recent findings regarding floating-point precision issues observed on A100 hardware.\n\nWe download models from Hugging Face and convert their weights from the Hugging Face format to the Megatron format:\n\n```bash\n# Qwen2.5-7B-Base\nhf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B --local-dir ../Qwen2.5-7B\nsource scripts/models/qwen2.5-7B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../Qwen2.5-7B \\\n    --save ../Qwen2.5-7B_torch_dist\n\n# R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B\nhf download deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B --local-dir ../DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B\nsource scripts/models/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B \\\n    --save ../DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B_torch_dist\n\n# DeepScaleR-1.5B\nhf download agentica-org/DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview --local-dir ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview\nsource scripts/models/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview \\\n    --save ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview_torch_dist\n\n# ProRL-1.5B-v2\nhf download nvidia/Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B --revision v2 --local-dir ../Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B-v2\nsource scripts/models/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B-v2 \\\n    --save ../Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B-v2_torch_dist\n\n# OpenThinker3-1.5B\nhf download open-thoughts/OpenThinker3-1.5B --local-dir ../OpenThinker3-1.5B\nsource scripts/models/qwen2.5-1.5B.sh\nPYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \\\n    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \\\n    --hf-checkpoint ../OpenThinker3-1.5B \\\n    --save ../OpenThinker3-1.5B_torch_dist\n```\n\n**Warning:** Please make sure the weight conversion is successful before starting any training.\nEven if the conversion fails, training can still launch without a runtime error, but the model will be trained from randomly initialized weights.\n\n\n## Reward Shaping\n\nBy default, we use the original reward provided by each verifiable environment as the reward used in the RL algorithm.  \nMany environments employ continuous reward shaping, meaning that a model output can still receive a positive reward even if its answer is not fully correct.  \nWe found that when the training scale is small, using a binary reward can sometimes yield slightly better results (i.e., the model output receives 1 if and only if its answer is fully correct, and 0 otherwise).  \nYou can switch to binary rewards by changing `--reward-key reward` to `--reward-key accuracy` in `scripts/training/[MODEL]/rlve.sh`.\n\n## Wandb Setup\n\nTo use Weights & Biases (wandb), please set your wandb API key in the environment variable `WANDB_API_KEY`.  \nAlternatively, you can comment out the wandb-related arguments in `WANDB_ARGS` within the training script to disable wandb.\n\n## Environment Scaling\n\nYou can run our environment scaling experiments as follows:\n\n```bash\n# Qwen2.5-7B-Base\nbash If that yields nothing, fall back to scanning the raw output line-by-\n           line (last line that looks like a whitespace-separated integer list).\n\n        Once indices are obtained:\n        * If parsing fails or indices are invalid (out-of-range, duplicates) → -1.0\n        * If deleting those indices does **not** reduce LNDS length by ≥ 1 → -1.0\n        * Otherwise:\n            score = 2·(optimal_cost / actual_cost) – 1\n          which yields +1.0 when actual = optimal and approaches -1.0 as the\n          submitted cost grows without bound.\n        \"\"\"\n        indices = self._extract_indices(output)\n        if indices is None:\n            return -1.0\n\n        # --- validity checks ---\n        if len(set(indices)) != len(indices):          # duplicates\n            return -1.0\n        for idx in indices:\n            if not (0 <= idx < self.N):                # out of range\n                return -1.0\n\n        # --- does it actually reduce the LNDS? ---\n        delete_set = set(indices)\n        remaining_A = [self.A[i] for i in range(self.N) if i not in delete_set]\n        new_lns = _compute_lns_length(remaining_A)\n        if new_lns >= self._original_lns:\n            return -1.0\n\n        actual_cost = sum(self.B[i] for i in indices)\n\n        # --- score from cost ratio ---\n        optimal = self._optimal_cost\n        if optimal == 0:\n            return 1.0 if actual_cost == 0 else -1.0\n\n        ratio = optimal / actual_cost          # in (0, 1]\n        score = 2.0 * ratio - 1.0              # in (-1, +1]\n        return max(-1.0, min(1.0, score))\n\n    def _extract_indices(self, output: str) -> Optional[List[int]]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Extract the list of indices from the model's raw output.\n\n        First tries the standard ``processor`` (which looks for\n        ``<answer>…</answer>`` tags).  If that returns ``None``, falls back to\n        a heuristic scan of the raw text.\n        \"\"\"\n        # 1 — try the tagged answer path\n        processed = self.processor(output)\n        if processed is not None and isinstance(processed, list):\n            return processed\n\n        # 2 — fallback: scan lines for index-looking patterns\n        text = output\n        # Strip \"Assistant:\" prefix if present (same logic as base class)\n        if \"Assistant:\" in text:\n            text = text.split(\"Assistant:\", 1)[1]\n        elif \"<|im_start|>assistant\" in text:\n            text = text.split(\"<|im_start|>assistant\", 1)[1]\n\n        lines = text.splitlines()\n        # Search backwards — last such line is most likely the answer\n        for line in reversed(lines):\n            line = line.strip()\n            if not line:\n                continue\n\n            # Strategy A: whole line is only digits and whitespace\n            if re.fullmatch(r'[0-9\\s]+', line):\n                parsed = self._parse_indices(line)\n                if parsed is not None:\n                    return parsed\n\n            # Strategy B: the line ends with a sequence of space-separated\n            # digits (e.g. \"The answer is: 0 1 2\" or \"indices: 3, 4, 5\")\n            m = re.search(r'(?:^|\\s)((?:\\d+\\s+)*\\d+)\\s*$', line)\n            if m:\n                parsed = self._parse_indices(m.group(1))\n                if parsed is not None:\n                    return parsed\n\n            # Strategy C: strip trailing non-digit suffix\n            # (e.g. \"1 2 3.\" → \"1 2 3\")\n            cleaned = re.sub(r'[^0-9\\s]+$', '', line).strip()\n            if cleaned and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9\\s]+', cleaned):\n                parsed = self._parse_indices(cleaned)\n                if parsed is not None:\n                    return parsed\n\n        return None\n","numLines":368,"startLine":1,"totalLines":368}}}

When reporting a problem, provide detailed information so we can assist you more effectively.\n    31→\n    32→## Setup\n    33→\n    34→Our environment setup is the same as the setup of the official [slime](https://github.com/THUDM/slime) framework. We use Docker:\n    35→\n    36→```bash\n    37→# Pull the image\n    38→docker pull slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126\n    39→\n    40→# Start the container\n    41→docker run -d --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \\\n    42→  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \\\n    43→  --name RLVE \\\n    44→  slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126 \\\n    45→  tail -f /dev/null\n    46→```\n    47→\n    48→After entering the Docker container, please follow these steps to clone the repository and install it:\n    49→\n    50→```bash\n    51→cd /root/\n    52→git clone https://github.com/Zhiyuan-Zeng/RLVE.git\n    53→cd RLVE\n    54→pip install -e .\n    55→```\n    56→\n    57→## Usage of Verifiable Environments in RLVE-Gym\n    58→\n    59→Each environment has an identifier, which you can find [here](Gym/environments/__init__.py). We take the following example:\n    60→\n    61→```python\n    62→identifier = \"Sorting\"\n    63→```\n    64→\n    65→Each environment has two classes - one for the environment itself and another for controlling the problem difficulty:\n    66→\n    67→```python\n    68→from Gym.environments import identifier2environment\n    69→from Gym.parameter_controllers import identifier2controller\n    70→\n    71→environment = identifier2environment[identifier]\n    72→controller_class = identifier2controller[identifier]\n    73→```\n    74→\n    75→Note that when creating the environment, you can specify the argument `answer_markers` to control how the answer is extracted from a model’s output during verification.\n    76→By default, it extracts the answer enclosed between `<answer>` and `</answer>`.\n    77→You can check [this example usage](slime/rollout/rm_hub/rlve_rm.py) for reference.\n    78→\n    79→When generating a problem, we specify a random seed `seed` and a problem difficulty level `d` ($d \\geq 0$):\n    80→\n    81→```python\n    82→import random\n    83→\n    84→seed = 42\n    85→\n    86→controller = controller_class()\n    87→d = 3\n    88→for _ in range(d) :\n    89→    controller.update()\n    90→\n    91→problem = environment()\n    92→parameter = random.choice(controller.get_parameter_list())\n    93→if problem.generator(seed = seed, parameter = parameter) :\n    94→    pass\n    95→else :\n    96→    problem = None\n    97→```\n    98→\n    99→Problem generation is successful when `problem` is not `None`.\n   100→\n   101→The input prompt is obtained via `problem.prompt_generator()`.  \n   102→The reward for a model output `output` is given by `problem.scorer(output)`, or you can access more detailed verification information using `problem.verifier(output)`.\n   103→\n   104→You can check [here](Gym/environment.py) for more detailed usage.\n   105→\n   106→## Model Download & Weight Conversion\n   107→\n   108→In the following, we assume you are on a node with 8 GPUs, each equipped with at least 80GB of memory.\n   109→We recommend using H100 or H200 GPUs over A100s, due to recent findings regarding floating-point precision issues observed on A100 hardware.\n   110→\n   111→We download models from Hugging Face and convert their weights from the Hugging Face format to the Megatron format:\n   112→\n   113→```bash\n ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview \\\n   136→    --save ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview_torch_dist\n   137→\n   138→# ProRL-1.5B-v2\n   139→hf download nvidia/Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B --revision v2 --local-dir ../Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B-v2\n   140→source scripts/models/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5B.sh\n   141→PYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py 155→**Warning:** Please make sure the weight conversion is successful before starting any training.\n   156→Even if the conversion fails, training can still launch without a runtime error, but the model will be trained from randomly initialized weights.\n   157→\n   158→\n   159→## Reward Shaping\n   160→\n   161→By default, we use the original reward provided by each verifiable environment as the reward used in the RL algorithm.  \n   162→Many environments employ continuous reward shaping, meaning that a model output can still receive a positive reward even if its answer is not fully correct.  \n   163→We found that when the training scale is small, using a binary reward can sometimes yield slightly better results (i.e., the model output receives 1 if and only if its answer is fully correct, and 0 otherwise).  \n   164→You can switch to binary rewards by changing `--reward-key reward` to `--reward-key accuracy` in `scripts/training/[MODEL]/rlve.sh`.\n   165→\n   166→## Wandb Setup\n   167→\n   168→To use Weights & Biases (wandb), please set your wandb API key in the environment variable `WANDB_API_KEY`.  \n   169→Alternatively, you can comment out the wandb-related arguments in `WANDB_ARGS` within the training script to disable wandb.\n   170→\n   171→## Environment Scaling\n   172→\n   173→You can run our environment scaling experiments as follows:\n   174→\n We use Docker:\n\n```bash\n# Pull the image\ndocker pull slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126\n\n# Start the container\ndocker run -d --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \\\n  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \\\n  --name RLVE \\\n  slimerl/slime:v0.5.0rc0-cu126 \\\n  tail -f /dev/null\n```\n\nAfter entering the Docker container, please follow these steps to clone the repository and install it:\n\n```bash\ncd /root/\ngit clone https://github.com/Zhiyuan-Zeng/RLVE.git\ncd RLVE\npip install -e .\n```\n\n## Usage of Verifiable Environments in RLVE-Gym\n\nEach environment has an identifier, which you can find [here](Gym/environments/__init__.py). We take the following example:\n\n```python\nidentifier = \"Sorting\"\n```\n\nEach environment has two classes - one for the environment itself and another for controlling the problem difficulty:\n\n```python\nfrom Gym.environments import identifier2environment\nfrom Gym.parameter_controllers import identifier2controller\n\nenvironment = identifier2environment[identifier]\ncontroller_class = identifier2controller[identifier]\n```\n\nNote that when creating the environment, you can specify the argument `answer_markers` to control how the answer is extracted from a model’s output during verification.\nBy default, it extracts the answer enclosed between `<answer>` and `</answer>`.\nYou can check [this example usage](slime/rollout/rm_hub/rlve_rm.py) for reference.\n\nWhen generating a problem, we specify a random seed `seed` and a problem difficulty level `d` ($d \\geq 0$):\n\n```python\nimport random\n\nseed = 42\n\ncontroller = controller_class()\nd = 3\nfor _ in range(d) :\n    controller.update()\n\nproblem = environment()\nparameter = random.choice(controller.get_parameter_list())\nif problem.generator(seed = seed, parameter = parameter) :\n    pass\nelse :\n    problem = None\n```\n\nProblem generation is successful when `problem` is not `None`.\n\nThe input prompt is obtained via `problem.prompt_generator()`.  \nThe reward for a model output `output` is given by `problem.scorer(output)`, or you can access more detailed verification information using `problem.verifier(output)`.\n\nYou can check [here](Gym/environment.py) for more detailed usage.\n\n## Model Download & Weight Conversion\n\nIn the following, we assume you are on a node with 8 GPUs, each equipped with at least 80GB of memory.\nWe recommend using H100 or H200 GPUs over A100s, due to recent findings regarding floating-point precision issues observed on A100 hardware.\n\nWe download ../Qwen2.5-7B_torch_dist\n\n# R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B\nhf download deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B --local-dir ../DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B\nsource \\\n    --save ../DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B_torch_dist\n\n# DeepScaleR-1.5B\nhf download agentica-org/DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview --local-dir ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview\nsource   --save ../DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview_torch_dist\n\n# ProRL-1.5B-v2\nhf download nvidia/Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B --revision v2 --local-dir ../OpenThinker3-1.5B \\\n    --save ../OpenThinker3-1.5B_torch_dist\n```\n\n**Warning:** Please make sure the weight conversion is successful before starting any training.\nEven if the conversion fails, training can still launch without a runtime error, but the model will be trained from randomly initialized weights.\n\n\n## Reward Shaping\n\nBy default, we use the original reward provided by each verifiable environment as the reward used in the RL algorithm.  \nMany environments employ continuous reward shaping, meaning that a model output can still receive a positive reward even if its answer is not fully correct.  \nWe found that when the training scale is small, using a binary reward can sometimes yield slightly better results (i.e., the model output receives 1 if and only if its answer is fully correct, and 0 otherwise).  \nYou can switch to binary rewards by changing `--reward-key reward` to `--reward-key accuracy` in `scripts/training/[MODEL]/rlve.sh`.\n\n## Wandb Setup\n\nTo use Weights & Biases (wandb), please set your wandb API key in the environment variable `WANDB_API_KEY`.  \nAlternatively, you can comment out the wandb-related arguments in `WANDB_ARGS` within the training script to disable wandb.\n\n## Environment Scaling\n\nYou can run our environment scaling experiments as follows:\n\n```bash\n# Qwen2.5-7B-Base\nbash Writes `pre.json` (passed list) + `pre_report.json`.\n- `data/SCAN_GRPO/prompts_8.json` (2.8MB) contains 8 prompts per environment; `prompts_8_failed.json` is empty `[]`.\n\n### Launcher scripts\n- **`/workspace/scripts/training/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct/rlve.sh`** — The main training launcher. **Hardcodes `LOCKED_ENVIRONMENT_LIST=\"MinCostReducingLNDS\"`** (regardless of the 3rd CLI arg). Each controller is in its own subdirectory with `__init__.py` + `parameter_controller.py`.\n- **`/workspace/Gym/environments/__init__.py`** — Registers only `identifier2environment = {\"MinCostReducingLNDS\": MinCostReducingLNDS_Environment}`.\n\n### The slime RL framework (RLVE-relevant bits)\n- **`/workspace/slime/utils/arguments.py`** — `parse_args()`; includes RLVE-specific args: `--rlve`, `--environment-list`, `--difficulty`, `--difficulty-window-size`, `--difficulty-increase-threshold` (lines ~846-879).\n- **`/workspace/slime/ray/buffer.py`** — GRPO advantage normalization (lines 105-110):\n  ```python\n  mean = rewards.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n  rewards = rewards - mean\n  if self.args.advantage_estimator in [\"grpo\", \"gspo\"] and self.args.grpo_std_normalization:\n      std = rewards.std(dim=-1, keepdim=True)\n      rewards = rewards / (std + 1e-6)\n  ```\n- **`/workspace/slime/rollout/rm_hub/rlve_rm.py`** — the RLVE reward model: builds `VerifiableEnvironment` from `metadata[\"environment\"]`/`metadata[\"config\"]` and returns `problem.verifier(response)`.\n- **`/workspace/slime/rollout/sglang_rollout.py`** — rollout + eval generation; contains the **SCAN_GRPO eval dump** block (lines ~454-491) that writes per-sample rewards+metadata to `RLVE_SCAN_EVAL_DUMP`.\n- **`/workspace/slime/rollout/rm_hub/__init__.py`** — `async_rm()` dispatcher (math/bbeh/livecodebench/rlve).\n\n### Custom SCAN-GRPO scripts\n- **`/workspace/scripts/build_scan_eval_json.py`** — For each environment, generates `N` eval prompts with metadata (uses `identifier2controller` + `identifier2environment`), writing `prompts_8.json` and `prompts_8_failed.json`.\n- **`/workspace/scripts/analyze_scan_eval.py`** — Reads the eval dump, groups samples per `environment::seed::prompt_idx`, computes `centered = r - mean; adv = centered/(std+1e-6)`, and reports which environments have **nonzero GRPO advantages** (i.e. would produce a training signal). Writes `pre.json` (passed list) + `pre_report.json`.\n- `data/SCAN_GRPO/prompts_8.json` (2.8MB) contains 8 prompts per environment; `prompts_8_failed.json` is empty `[]`.\n\n### Launcher scripts\n- **`/workspace/scripts/training/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct/rlve.sh`** — The main training launcher. **Hardcodes `LOCKED_ENVIRONMENT_LIST=\"MinCostReducingLNDS\"`** (regardless of the 3rd CLI arg). Sets up checkpoint/rollout/eval/perf/GRPO/optimizer/wandb arg arrays, derives GPU count from `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, computes a deterministic Ray port namespace keyed by GPU signature, starts Ray head, then `ray job submit -- python3 train.py ...`. Logs go to `logs/{RUN_NAME}/run_{TS}/{launcher,ray_job}.log`.\n- **`/workspace/scripts/training/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct/rlve_scan.sh`** — SCAN variant. **Hardcodes `LOCKED_ENVIRONMENT_LIST=\"MinimumCost_MaximumFlow\"`** (note: this environment is **not** registered in `Gym/environments/__init__.py`, so it would fail at runtime unless the env registry is populated). Passes `RLVE_SCAN_GRPO`, `RLVE_SCAN_EVAL_DUMP`, `RLVE_SCAN_PRE_JSON`, `RLVE_SCAN_REPORT_JSON` into the Ray runtime env. Uses `--num-rollout 1`, `--eval-interval 1`, `--eval-prompt-data SCAN_GRPO data/SCAN_GRPO/prompts_8.json`, and no wandb.\n- **`rlve/num-environment={1,4,16,256}.sh`** — wrappers that call `rlve.sh` with different environment lists (4 envs, 16 envs, 256 envs, and `PolyaModel` for the 1-env case). Note: `num-environment=1.sh` passes `PolyaModel` but `rlve.sh` overrides it to `MinCostReducingLNDS`.\n\n---\n\n## 6.
